problem: Source: 'he would make me sensible that it was a superfluity, unrequired by him, unbecoming in me.' Modern 'unwanted and excessive. Superfluous.' drops 'unbecoming in me' (the feeling would be improper in her, not merely excessive) and adds a stray fragment; the earlier 'Because he is so talented...' is also detached from its main clause.
new_text: "And then," I continued, "though I feel only sisterly affection for him now, if forced to be his wife, I can imagine developing an unavoidable, strange, agonizing kind of love for him, because he is so talented, and there's often a certain heroic grandeur in his look, manner, and conversation. In that case, my life would become unspeakably wretched. He wouldn't want me to love him. And if I showed the feeling, he'd make me understand that it was superfluous—something he didn't require and that was unbecoming in me. I know he would."

problem: Source: 'I should not the less be made to repent, some day, of my former rebellion.' Modern drops 'some day' and softens 'rebellion' to 'resistance'; the delayed, inevitable reckoning is lost.
new_text: "Could you decide now?" asked the missionary. The question was put gently. He drew me to him, also gently. Oh, that gentleness! How much more powerful it was than force! I could resist St. John's anger. But I grew soft as a reed under his kindness. Yet I knew all the time that if I gave in now, I would still be made to repent, some day, of my earlier rebellion. His nature had not changed in one hour of solemn prayer. It was only lifted up.

problem: Source addresses superstition: 'This is not thy deception, nor thy witchcraft: it is the work of nature.' Modern 'This is not deception, nor witchcraft' drops the possessive, so it denies deception altogether rather than denying that superstition is responsible.
new_text: "Down, superstition!" I told myself, as that phantom rose up dark beside the black yew tree at the gate. "This is not your deception, nor your witchcraft. It is the work of nature. She was stirred, and she did—no miracle—but her best."
